name: Mangrove
notes: Intertidal salt-tolerant forest: stilt-rooted Rhizophora on the seaward edge, pneumatophore-bearing Avicennia/Sonneratia, Laguncularia/Bruguiera landward, nipa palm and ferns at the freshwater fringe. Drawn on the Atlantic-East Pacific (Florida, Caribbean, W Africa) and Indo-West Pacific (Sundarbans, SE Asia, N Australia) mangrove provinces.

canopy.name: Red mangrove
canopy.source: Rhizophora mangle, red mangrove, prop-rooted seaward pioneer of Atlantic/E Pacific mangroves, 5-20 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Asian stilt mangrove
canopy.source: Rhizophora mucronata, loop-root mangrove, dominant seaward Rhizophora of Indo-West Pacific coasts, 8-25 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Black mangrove
canopy.source: Avicennia germinans, black mangrove, pencil-pneumatophore species of the mid-intertidal, Atlantic Americas/W Africa, 3-15 m; A. marina its Indo-Pacific counterpart — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Grey mangrove
canopy.source: Avicennia marina, grey/white mangrove, most widespread and cold-tolerant mangrove of the Indo-West Pacific (to NZ, Red Sea), 3-14 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: White mangrove
canopy.source: Laguncularia racemosa, white mangrove, landward-zone mangrove of Atlantic/E Pacific coasts, 3-12 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Mangrove apple
canopy.source: Sonneratia alba, mangrove apple, cone-pneumatophore pioneer of Indo-Pacific mangrove seaward fringe, 5-15 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Nipa palm
shrub.source: Nypa fruticans, nipa palm, trunkless palm of brackish tidal creeks in Indo-West Pacific mangroves, fronds 4-9 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Buttonwood
shrub.source: Conocarpus erectus, buttonwood, mangrove-associate shrub of the upper tidal edge, tropical Americas/W Africa, 2-10 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Orange mangrove
shrub.source: Bruguiera gymnorhiza, large-leafed orange mangrove, knee-rooted landward mangrove of Indo-West Pacific, 5-20 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Holly mangrove
shrub.source: Acanthus ilicifolius, sea holly, spiny-leaved shrub of Indo-Pacific mangrove understory and creek banks, 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Mangrove fern
shrub.source: Acrostichum aureum, golden leather fern, giant fern of brackish mangrove back-swamps pantropically, 1-3 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Mangrove seedling
ground.source: Rhizophora mangle propagule/seedling, planted spears on tidal mudflat — Wikipedia

ground.name: Saltwort
ground.source: Batis maritima, saltwort, succulent mat on hypersaline pans behind Americas mangroves, 0.1-0.5 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Sea purslane
ground.source: Sesuvium portulacastrum, shoreline sea purslane, pantropical succulent creeper on mangrove mud and sand, prostrate — Wikipedia

ground.name: Smooth cordgrass
ground.source: Sporobolus (Spartina) alterniflorus, smooth cordgrass, tidal marsh grass at the mangrove/salt-marsh ecotone, Atlantic Americas, 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Turtle grass
ground.source: Thalassia testudinum, turtle grass, seagrass meadow seaward of Caribbean/Gulf mangroves, 0.2-0.6 m blades — Wikipedia (underwater)

epiphyte.name: Mangrove orchid
epiphyte.source: Dendrobium crumenatum, pigeon orchid, epiphyte on Indo-Malesian mangrove and coastal trees — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Mangrove bromeliad
epiphyte.source: Tillandsia utriculata, giant air plant, epiphyte on black/red mangrove branches in Florida and Caribbean — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Ant plant
epiphyte.source: Myrmecodia beccarii, ant-house plant, tuberous epiphyte on Queensland mangrove trunks — Wikipedia
